evidence.source_name: Statistics Bureau of Japan, 2021 Survey on Time Use and Leisure Activities, Questionnaire A, Table 1-1
evidence.scope: Table 1-1 reports 2021 total weekly-average daily time for Sports as 0.13 Hours.minutes, meaning 0 hours 13 minutes per average day. Population: people living in Japan aged 10 years and over. The outline reports about 190,000 surveyed household members of this age; Questionnaire A is used in around 7,152 of 7,576 enumeration districts.
evidence.limitations: All-person mean time for a broad category, not participant rate or count of participants, episodes, objects or primitives. Questionnaire A records main activity in 15-minute slots; simultaneous secondary activities are not reported as the main activity. No YCB object, specific sport, ball interaction or robot task is identified. 0.13 means 13 minutes, not decimal hours. No sports-specific sample count is reported, so observed_count is null.
evidence.notes: Primary source, official Table 1-1 total 2021 column, Sports row. Opening text defines values as daily time averaged over a week and covered population as people aged 10+. Survey outline: https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/shakai/2021/gaiyo.html. It describes two diary days in a nine-day window, a two-stage stratified sample and exclusions including institutional residents and hospital inpatients.

evidence.source_name: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Explanation of Terms for the 2021 Survey, Questionnaire A
evidence.scope: Questionnaire A uses 20 predetermined time-use categories; Sports is one tertiary activity. Respondents report their main activity in 15-minute slots.
evidence.limitations: Defines a broad source category for a macro-activity crosswalk only. It does not specify an object, sport, motor primitive, performance outcome or robot procedure and does not itself support a population-frequency value.
evidence.notes: Primary survey coding documentation, used only to justify representation of the official category.

evidence.source_name: Stanford BEHAVIOR Knowledgebase, ball.n.01 and its soccer_ball.n.01 and softball.n.01 children
evidence.source_version: Knowledgebase pages accessed 2026-09-25; web version not release-pinned
evidence.scope: The knowledgebase defines ball.n.01 as a round object hit, thrown or kicked in games and lists soccer_ball.n.01 and softball.n.01 as children. Used as broad rationale for candidate tasks with YCB mini soccer ball and softball.
evidence.limitations: Taxonomy supports only a proposed relationship between sports balls and candidate tasks; it does not specify these Atlas procedures, establish YCB taxonomy equivalence, prove execution or provide population frequency. Proposals use stationary pickup/place/recovery rather than throwing or kicking.
evidence.notes: Primary pages: https://behavior.stanford.edu/knowledgebase/synsets/ball.n.01.html; https://behavior.stanford.edu/knowledgebase/synsets/soccer_ball.n.01.html; https://behavior.stanford.edu/knowledgebase/synsets/softball.n.01.html. Mapping to Atlas concept object_ball is curator-authored.

evidence.source_name: YCB Object and Model Set official object catalog
evidence.scope: Catalog lists 053_mini_soccer_ball and 054_softball, with processed, RGB and RGB-D data package links.
evidence.limitations: Catalog establishes source identifiers and data availability only; no human activity frequency, task suitability, robot performance or simulator compatibility.
evidence.notes: Official YCB index. The two identifiers map to existing Atlas ObjectInstances ycb_053_mini_soccer_ball and ycb_054_softball. Their shared object_ball class is a separate curator grouping.
